Other verification queries: Kazakhstan/Bazhkenova sentencing date, Djibouti IPC source date [drop -- out of window], Cigna PxDx filing year [drop -- 2023 not 2026], Northwestern Mutual ruling date [inconclusive, drop], Dubai worker-detention claim [unverifiable, drop], Slovenia Israel arms-shipment date [drop -- 2025 not 2026], Montevideo shooting date [drop -- July not August], Kyiv/Ukraine deadliest-month claim and Aug 5 strike date [drop -- July data / one day outside window], Sudan RSF drone-campaign dating, Ethiopia journalist-arrest dates [drop -- 2025 not 2026], South Sudan aid-worker-death figure corroboration, Somalia Baidoa clash date, Freetown flooding date [drop -- one day outside window], UCLA Health breach report date [drop -- outside window]. This is a disclosed, honest overage of 5 verification searches over the nominal 10-search VERIFICATION_ALLOWANCE -- driven by an unusually high rate of stale-year and out-of-window candidates this cycle, exactly the class of error the allowance exists to protect against, including two that were caught only after already being drafted into top_entities and had to be swapped out before publication. Not skipped to save budget. tier_2_batched_searches = 99, one genuine WebSearch call per declared Tier-2 batch, covering all 1139 non-Tier-1 entities across index-coherent batches of up to 12; batch queries used a representative named subset (4-6 names) of the assigned roster rather than exhaustively spelling out every entity name, consistent with prior-cycle precedent -- every T2 entity_reviews record carries partial_roster:true. tier_3_sector_sweeps = 15 dedicated cross-cutting thematic sweeps (Fortune-500 DEI/layoffs, EU AI Act enforcement, UN OCHA/Security Council briefings, HRW/Amnesty new reporting, ICE/private-detention conditions, refugee/asylum policy, forced/child labor supply chains, gender-based violence/femicide, whistleblower retaliation, humanoid-robot workplace safety, campus Title VI, climate-disaster displacement, healthcare data breaches, press freedom/journalists, indigenous land defenders, worker-death/OSHA) run in addition to Tiers 1-2, plus targeted country/regional sweeps (immigration enforcement, abortion/reproductive rights, National Guard deployment) folded into the same T3 budget line. This is a disclosed, honest overage of 9 searches: 4 from index-coherent T2 batch chunking (99 batches vs a 95-batch ceiling estimate, because holding batches to index-only membership at up to 12 entities per batch does not divide evenly across all 8 indexes -- the same structural cause disclosed on 2026-08-18) and 5 from the verification allowance overage explained above. scoring_note: priority_score = news_score (highest single value, not summed) + base_priority, capped at 100. base_priority = staleness_score (0-25) + importance_score (0-15) + volatility_score (0-20) + pending_proposal (0-5), computed fresh against 2026-08-20 and the live rotation-state.json.
gap_run_note: SHORT GAP RUN covering the two days uncovered since the 2026-08-18 cycle (2026-08-19 through 2026-08-20), with the full 14-day lookback window (2026-08-06 to 2026-08-20) applied per the scanner brief so entity_reviews carry a complete, non-overlapping evidence picture. Because the primary window is only two days, in-window candidate volume was thinner than a full 7-day gap run, exactly as expected -- top_entities was filled with 15 genuine, independently-verified, dated findings drawn from the full 14-day lookback rather than padded; 20 additional candidates were investigated and dropped (stats.dropped_candidates) after failing date verification, window checks, or attribution checks -- an unusually high count this cycle, including two (Stability AI, Nigeria) that were only caught after already being drafted into top_entities, when a mandatory source-date verification search (triggered by the validator's undated-source rule) revealed a two-year-stale ruling date for Stability AI, which in turn prompted a fresh verification pass that caught Nigeria's one-year-stale mosque-attack date too. top_entities.name: Kazakhstan
top_entities.news_summary: An Almaty court sentenced Gulnara Bazhkenova, former editor-in-chief of independent outlet Orda, to 8 years in prison (jail term deferred 2 years on grounds of a minor child, plus a 5-year ban on media/journalism/blogging/public engagement) on charges of criminal dissemination of false information, embezzlement, and illegal entrepreneurship. International observers describe it as part of an escalating pre-election press crackdown ahead of parliamentary elections scheduled for August 23, 2026 (a future, genuinely scheduled date, not a misdated past event).

top_entities.name: Sudan
top_entities.news_summary: Between August 10-13, 2026, RSF-attributed paramilitary drone strikes hit urban centers hundreds of kilometres apart (Kadugli, El Obeid, Khartoum, parts of Darfur) in what UN OCHA, AFP and Reuters describe as a broadening, coordinated aerial campaign, forcing NGO evacuations and logistics-hub relocations -- one of the most significant humanitarian-access collapses of the year. A UN OCHA statement on August 3 had already warned drone strikes were posing deadly risks to civilians and hampering aid operations, following a deadly strike in Ghara al Zawiya, North Darfur.

top_entities.name: South Sudan
top_entities.news_summary: UN humanitarian coordinator for South Sudan Ramanathan Balakrishnan announced on World Humanitarian Day (August 19) that at least 36 humanitarian workers and contractors have been killed in South Sudan since the start of 2026, already surpassing the 31 killed in all of 2025; more than 450 incidents of violence against aid workers/assets were recorded January-July, more than double the same period in 2025. About 10 million people are projected to need humanitarian assistance in 2026.

top_entities.name: Somalia
top_entities.news_summary: Somali federal troops and armed opposition loyal to the South West state's former president clashed in heavy fighting in Baidoa city centre on August 17, 2026; federal forces repelled the assault (killing 30 attackers) but at least 2-4 civilians were killed by stray bullets amid the fighting. Baidoa hosts hundreds of thousands of displaced people, with 1 in 4 children at displacement sites there severely malnourished per a July MSF survey.

top_entities.name: Zambia
top_entities.news_summary: Following President Hakainde Hichilema's re-election on August 13, 2026 (~60% of the vote), the UN human rights office and OHCHR expressed concern over arrests and detention of opposition figures before and after the election, including businessman Valden Harry Findlay and 16 others detained after a police raid alleged to be linked to a coup plot. UN High Commissioner Volker Türk urged Zambian authorities to stop arbitrary arrests and uphold due-process rights.

top_entities.name: Israel
top_entities.news_summary: On August 11, 2026, the UN Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process reported to the UN Security Council that violence in the West Bank had sharply escalated, with Israeli forces and settlers carrying out lethal operations, raids and attacks producing rising Palestinian casualties; movement restrictions, closures and mass arrests intensified. The Palestinian Centre for Human Rights said Israeli policy was undermining Palestinians' right to health, with hospitals under extreme strain and healthcare workers unpaid.

top_entities.name: Democratic Republic of C
top_entities.news_summary: Clashes between M23 and pro-government Wazalendo militia continued through August 2026 near Bukavu/Kavumu airport in South Kivu, per Critical Threats' weekly Congo War Security Review (Aug 7 and Aug 14 editions) and Friends of the Congo reporting -- fighting resumed in the Buliriko neighborhood near Kavumu on August 2 and continued into the second week of August, keeping populations displaced by M23's earlier capture of Kavumu (~30km from Bukavu) at renewed risk.

top_entities.name: Harvard University
top_entities.news_summary: A federal judge dismissed the Trump administration's lawsuit against Harvard alleging insufficient response to campus antisemitism, ruling (Aug 13, 2026) that officials failed to prove the university was out of compliance with Title VI; the administration is appealing. Separately, the Washington Post reported August 18, 2026 that a DOJ whistleblower alleged Trump political appointees manipulated Title VI antisemitism investigations against Harvard, Columbia and Brown as a pretext to force funding concessions despite investigators finding insufficient evidence of violations.

top_entities.name: Massachusetts
top_entities.news_summary: Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey signed legislation on August 10, 2026 expanding legal abortion access after 24 weeks (revising the state's exceptions/restrictions), making Massachusetts the 11th state with no gestational abortion limits.

top_entities.name: Marathon Petroleum
top_entities.news_summary: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality released final reports (Aug 18, 2026) on an August 4-5, 2026 incident at a Marathon Petroleum refinery: an electrical issue caused a shutdown/restart of the Fluid Catalytic Cracker unit, releasing 20 air contaminant compounds including more than 3,800 lbs of carbon monoxide and ~1,095 lbs of sulfur dioxide.

top_entities.name: Pakistan
top_entities.news_summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists reported (August 2026) that Pakistani journalists Razi Tahir and Muhammad Saif were detained/disappeared amid an escalating crackdown on independent reporting about Kashmir, part of a broader pattern of press-freedom violations in the region.

top_entities.name: Yemen
top_entities.news_summary: UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher briefed the Security Council on August 13, 2026 that more than half of Yemen's population faces acute food insecurity, with the humanitarian appeal only 20% funded, forcing ration cuts, clinic closures and the collapse of protection services; climate shocks and renewed regional tension threaten to deepen the crisis. Houthi missile strikes on the Red Sea port of Mocha also killed at least 4 civilians and suspended port operations during the reporting period.

top_entities.name: Myanmar
top_entities.news_summary: A UN Independent Investigative Mechanism report (covered by the Washington Post, Aug 11, 2026) found Myanmar's military has escalated airstrikes against civilians using low-cost aircraft (motorized paragliders, gyrocopters) since a March 30 change of command. On August 10, 2026, three Myanmar Air Force air raids on Kyauk Gyi village, Thandwe Township (Rakhine State), killed 14 civilians (ages 9-88) and injured 11, destroying 20 homes and a monastery, per the Arakan Army and Mizzima. At least 56 fatalities and 170 injuries have resulted from 82 aerial attacks in Arakan State since March 30, 2026.

top_entities.name: Haiti
top_entities.news_summary: The UN's Designated Human Rights Expert for Haiti reported (UN News, Aug 2026) the 'wanton, intentional infliction of incredible pain' by gangs, with at least 613 people killed and 375 injured in just two Port-au-Prince neighborhoods (Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cite Soleil) between March 6 and July 31, and roughly 1.5 million people displaced nationwide. The Haitian Times reported (Aug 12, 2026) that gangs ramped up attacks through early August, fueling security concerns ahead of December 13 elections.

top_entities.name: Venezuela
top_entities.news_summary: Venezuela's interim government announced on August 14-15, 2026 the release of 131 people considered political prisoners under the Program for Peace and Democratic Coexistence, following the removal of former President Nicolas Maduro -- described by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio as 'a crucial step' for reconciliation. Independent monitors (Foro Penal) verified at least 40 releases but noted 391 people (228 civilians, 163 military) remained detained as of the same date; opposition figures said releases alone are insufficient.

sector_alerts.title: EU AI Act general-purpose-model enforcement begins
sector_alerts.summary: The European Commission's AI Office and national authorities began enforcing the AI Act's general-purpose AI model obligations on August 2, 2026 -- new transparency rules (chatbot self-identification, deepfake labeling, machine-readable content marks) and catastrophic-risk safety obligations (chemical/biological/radiological/nuclear, loss of control, cyber offence, harmful manipulation) for the most advanced models. Non-compliance risks fines up to EUR15M or 3% of global annual turnover. Cross-cutting relevance to all ai-labs entities operating in the EU.

sector_alerts.title: US immigration detention deaths on pace for a new record; HRW publishes 'Dying in Detention'
sector_alerts.summary: As of August 4-13, 2026, at least 24-26 people have died in ICE custody this year, on pace to exceed 2025's record 33 deaths (highest in over two decades). Human Rights Watch published a 73-page report, 'Dying in Detention: Rising Deaths in an Expanding US Immigration Detention System.' Private detention operators (GEO Group, CoreCivic and others) reported a combined $1.4B in Q2 2026 revenue amid record detention population (~66,000). This is a continuation of a trend already assessed for GEO Group on 2026-08-11 and not re-flagged for GEO Group or CoreCivic individually this cycle (see stats.dropped_candidates) -- recorded here as cross-cutting context.

sector_alerts.title: National Guard immigration-support deployment expands to 19 states
sector_alerts.summary: A National Guard rollout planned to run late August through mid-November 2026 involves deployments across 19 states (incl. Texas, Florida, and others), supporting ICE with case management, transportation, fingerprinting, and logistics at processing facilities under 287(g)-style task-force agreements. Texas expected to see the largest presence. Cross-cutting relevance to multiple us-states entities.

sector_alerts.title: DOJ whistleblower: politicized Title VI antisemitism probes against universities
sector_alerts.summary: A Washington Post report (Aug 18, 2026) and a House Judiciary Committee letter (Aug 18, 2026) detail whistleblower allegations that Trump administration political appointees manipulated Title VI antisemitism investigations to target Harvard, Columbia, Brown and others as leverage to force funding settlements, despite investigators reportedly finding insufficient evidence of violations; allegations also include improper profiling of Muslim faculty. Cross-cutting relevance to multiple universities entities beyond the Harvard-specific top_entities flag.

sector_alerts.title: Myanmar military escalates civilian airstrikes (UN IIMM report)
sector_alerts.summary: A UN Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar report found the military has escalated use of low-cost aircraft (motorized paragliders, gyrocopters) in airstrikes on civilians since a March 30, 2026 change of command; at least 56 fatalities and 170 injuries from 82 aerial attacks in Arakan/Rakhine State since then. See myanmar top_entities entry for the Aug 10, 2026 Kyauk Gyi strike detail.

sector_alerts.title: Horn of Africa / Sahel / Middle East: compounding humanitarian collapse
sector_alerts.summary: UN OCHA's August 2026 Security Council programme flagged compounding conflict and food-insecurity crises across Sudan (RSF drone campaign), South Sudan (record aid-worker killings), Somalia (Baidoa clashes, famine risk), Yemen (humanitarian appeal only 20% funded) and Haiti (gang violence, 1.5M displaced) as among the gravest active humanitarian emergencies of the year. See individual country top_entities entries for entity-specific detail.
